Triage: lands in `packages/client/src/index.ts` ⇒ **`domain:cli`** (unchanged); **type `Bug`, `priority:p2`, `finding` → `pm:queue`.**

## Grading

**Class (b) — violates a declared contract, and the card quotes the contract text.** `BaseResponseSchema` declares `success: z.boolean()` with no `.optional()` and no `.default()`, and `SessionResponseSchema.data` requires `session`. Both methods annotate their return as `SessionResponse` and deliver neither. That is the declared-contract class on the return side, measured through a real `AuthManager` rather than argued from the source.

**Dispatchable, not a decision.** This is the mechanical-boundary test in its clean form: the fix **pulls the implementation back to a contract that is already declared**. It does not widen the accepted set and does not touch a published shape — `SessionResponseSchema` is not edited, it is finally satisfied. ⇒ Work lane, not the decision box.

⚠️ **Scope fence for the dispatch, so nobody widens it into the sibling.** This card is sign-in and sign-up — the authenticated result, where a session genuinely exists. It is **not** #17238, which is the anonymous case and whose only fixes change a published contract; that one is in the decision box. ⛔ Do not fold them: same route family, different defect shape, and one of the two is unruled. That fails folding gate ③ before it reaches any of the others.

⚠️ **The premise a dev must falsify first:** the card says better-auth returns a bare `{ token, user }` with no `session`, so delivering `data.session` is not a matter of copying a field that is already in hand. Measure what the sign-in response actually carries before choosing between deriving the session and fetching it. If it turns out no session is obtainable on that path without a second call, ⛔ stop and report rather than inventing one — that would change the shape rather than satisfy it.

`priority:p2`: the two most common auth calls in the SDK, wrong against their own declared type, on every consumer that narrows on it — but nothing a signed-in user sees breaks today, because JavaScript does not check. Not p1.

`priority` and `pm:` state were correctly left unset by the filing seat; `finding` comes off in this same write.

This is the oldest `Bug`/p2 in the lane.

---

## 1. The ruling that bounds this card

Triage ruled it at [`5621312285`](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/17234#issuecomment-5621312285), and the ruling is the fence, not a suggestion. Quoted:

> **Dispatchable, not a decision.** This is the mechanical-boundary test in its clean form: the fix **pulls the implementation back to a contract that is already declared**. It does not widen the accepted set and does not touch a published shape — `SessionResponseSchema` is not edited, it is finally satisfied.

> ⚠️ **Scope fence for the dispatch, so nobody widens it into the sibling.** This card is sign-in and sign-up — the authenticated result, where a session genuinely exists. It is **not** #17238 … ⛔ Do not fold them.

> ⚠️ **The premise a dev must falsify first:** … Measure what the sign-in response actually carries before choosing between deriving the session and fetching it. If it turns out no session is obtainable on that path without a second call, ⛔ stop and report rather than inventing one — that would change the shape rather than satisfy it.

Standing protocol clause that applies here: 「凡触 `packages/spec` 一律转 `domain:spec` 座位,不论谁需要它」. ⇒ if your measurement says the only way out is to edit `SessionResponseSchema` or `BaseResponseSchema`, that is a **different seat's card**: ⛔ do not edit those files, stop and report.

#17238 is now `domain:services` + `pm:queue` (read 2026-09-12T04:45Z) — a different lane as well as a different defect. ⛔ Out of scope in both directions.

## 2. Premise check — done at dispatch, and still yours to falsify first

All three faces read against `origin/main` at 2026-09-12T04:45Z (fetched, not the working tree):

| face | command | result |
|:--|:--|:--|
| action | `git log --oneline -12 origin/main -- packages/client/src/index.ts` | tip `7baf04ae` (#17755, a docs-only OAuth change). Nothing touches `login`/`register`. |
| work item | `git show origin/main:packages/client/src/index.ts` | `login` (~`:4272`) and `register` (~`:4343`) both still carry the inline `const data = raw && (raw.data ?? …); const normalized = data ? { ...raw, data } : raw;`. **No `success` is written by either.** |
| card references | `GET /issues/{16760,17238}` | #16760 closed/`completed`; #17238 open, `domain:services`, `pm:queue`. (#14313 and #12104 in the card's `Refs:` line return HTTP 404 — dangling numbers, not work items.) |

⇒ **the premise holds.** Re-measure it yourself before writing code; if any of the three faces reads differently when you get there, that is a finding and a stop, not something to work around.

## 3. What "fixed" means here — two departures, judged separately

The card names two, and they do **not** have the same difficulty:

1. **`success` is absent.** `SessionResponseSchema` is `BaseResponseSchema.extend(…)`; that base declares `success: z.boolean()` with no `.optional()` and no `.default()`. `ObjectStackClient.unwrapResponse` keys on exactly this flag. This half is a straight pull-back to the declared contract.
2. **`data.session` is absent.** `/sign-in/email` and `/sign-up/email` answer `{ token, user }` (and `redirect` on sign-in). **This is the half the ruling tells you to measure before choosing**, and the half where inventing a value is forbidden.

⭐ There is a lift helper already in the file — `normalizeSessionResponse` at `:1505`, added by #16760 — and it is **not** a drop-in for these two routes. Read its docblock (`:1462`-`:1504`) before you reach for it. Two things in it are traps:

- It builds `data: { user: body.user, session: body.session }` and **nothing else**. `login` and `register` currently put the token at `data.token` and then auto-set `this.token` from it. Routing them through the helper unchanged **drops `data.token` and silently stops the auto-set** — a live regression on the most-used path in the SDK, in a PR whose whole point is fidelity.
- Its docblock states outright: 「**`data.token` is NOT synthesized from `session.token`**. The declared key is optional, and the two spellings are not one string: `session.token` is the UNSIGNED session token, while the `token` `login` puts there is the SIGNED `token.signature` form `bearer()` hands out.」 ⇒ ⛔ do not "fill" `data.token` from a session object, and ⛔ do not make `login`'s existing signed token into an unsigned one. Whatever you land must keep the credential currently at `data.token` byte-identical.

⚠️ That same docblock also says 「`auth.login` has carried the same lift for `/sign-in/email`'s own bare `{ token, user }` since long before this card」. Against the card's measurement that sentence is loose — login's inline version fills `data` but never `success`, which is precisely this defect. Check it; if your change makes the sentence true, leave it, and if it is still inaccurate afterwards, correct it in the same PR (same file, same subject) and say so in the PR body.

## 4. Acceptance — every item is a driven reading, ⛔ never a file listing or a type annotation

1. **Driven, not simulated.** Exercise both methods the way the card did: a real `AuthManager` (better-auth, organization plugin) over a real `ObjectQL` on a real driver, with an `ObjectStackClient` whose `fetch` is that manager. A hand-built fake response object proves nothing about what better-auth sends.
2. **`SessionResponseSchema.safeParse` on the value each method RETURNS.** Report the issue list for `login` and for `register`, before and after. The `success` issue must be gone in both.
3. **Controls that can fail.** (a) A negative control on the same instrument: a body you fabricate WITHOUT `success` must still fail the parse, so a green after-reading is a reading and not a broken assertion. (b) `data.token` before/after must be the same string, and `client.token` must still be set after `login` — pin both.
4. **`data.session`**: either deliver it with a measurement showing where the value legitimately comes from, or report, with the measurement, that it is not obtainable on that path without a second network call. ⛔ Never synthesize one. ⛔ Never relax the declaration.
5. **`auth.me` / `auth.refreshToken` are untouched** — `git diff` proof that #16760's work is not disturbed.
6. Tests land as a new or extended file in `packages/client`, and a `.changeset/` entry is required.

**How the two outcomes land, and this part is not the dev's discretion:**

- Both departures closed ⇒ PR body carries `Fixes #17234`.
- `success` closed but `data.session` proven unobtainable without a second call ⇒ the PR body carries **`Refs #17234`, ⛔ not `Fixes`**, states plainly in its own words that `data.session` is still undelivered, and the card stays open for the shape decision. A half-closed defect behind a closing keyword is the failure mode this rule exists to prevent.

## 5. Mechanics

- One worktree, branch exactly `claude/issue-17234-auth-login-register-envelope`. ⛔ Never edit the shared checkout, ⛔ never `git stash`.
- Open the PR as a **draft**.
- The PR body must carry a line beginning at column 0, bare, exactly `Clause-②: yes` or `Clause-②: no` — no bullet, no bold, no blockquote, no backticks. The PR-body reader is stricter than the card-side one and rejects decorated keys; a decorated key has already cost this lane one red gate.
- Run the repo's own fast checks before pushing (lint, typecheck, the changed package's tests) and report their exit codes.
- Report back with the `os-dev-report` JSON block. ⛔ Do not mark anything done that you did not measure; an absent measurement is reported as absent, never as a pass.

Clause-②: no

**Card-side clause-② carrier, owed by this seat and missing until now.** `domain:cli` execution seat (#6024), 2026-09-12T05:52Z. This is the declaration limb for card #17234 / PR #17791.

### Why this comment exists — a seat-template fault, measured

`node scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs --pair 17791` reports **exit 4, NOT clause-② legible**, and names the card side:

> NO READING on the declaration limb, and the PLACEMENT of the key is what is wrong, NOT its spelling: the thread carries the key in the fixed spelling … but not at the START of a line. … Remedy: put the `Clause-②: yes|no` line on a line of its OWN in the card's claim comment.

The dispatch order at [`5643501154`](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/17234#issuecomment-5643501154) mentions the key only **inside a prose bullet instructing the dev about the PR body** — so the card side declared nothing at all. ⚠️ ⛔ A missing reading is **not** a declared `no`: one is a decision, the other is an absent one. This comment supplies the decision.

⭐ This is a template regression in this seat's own claim format, ⛔ not a typo on one card. An earlier claim from this seat ([`5634883930`](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/17329#issuecomment-5634883930) on #17329) carried a bare `Clause-②:` line on its own; the compact one-line claim used this round dropped it. **#17620 is dispatched with the same template and is being fixed in the same pass.**

⚠️ One correction to the report that surfaced this. The dev diagnosed it as a missing `Branch:` line making the claim parse to zero branches, and reported the script exiting **2 / UNJUDGED**. Run here, the script exits **4** and names the *declaration* limb, not branch parsing. The finding was right and valuable; the mechanism it named was not, and the remedy differs. ⭐ Reported out rather than quietly corrected, because a wrong mechanism sends the next reader to the wrong line.

### The judgement — `no`, and why

The dispatched work makes `auth.login` / `auth.register` **satisfy a type they already advertise**. `SessionResponseSchema` and `BaseResponseSchema` are untouched; nothing authorable moves; no flag, route, envelope code or exit vocabulary is added. Filling a `success` the declaration already requires is the 拉回已声明契约 direction, which is the non-floor side of the mechanical boundary test. ⇒ `no`.

⚠️ **Scope of this declaration.** It covers the work this claim dispatched — the `success` half. The still-undelivered half (`data.session`) is measured unobtainable on these two routes without a second call, and how to resolve it is a published-contract question this seat ⛔ does not answer. That half goes to the decision box with its own four-axis block, and whatever is dispatched for it later carries **its own** clause-② declaration. ⛔ This `no` does not travel to it.

Card #17234 named **two** departures from the `SessionResponse` these two methods declare. ⇒ the directive names the test (*is the spec itself genuinely wrong?*) and the cost of answering yes (*deliberately — edit the Zod schema + migrate*). ## Protocol declaration

Option **B** changes `packages/spec` ⇒ 「凡触 `packages/spec` 一律转 `domain:spec` 座位,不论谁需要它」, so B is executed by that seat, not this one, whoever asks for it. Options A and C do not change the protocol. All three are above this seat's confidence gate: a published contract's shape is a manual floor.

## Premise, with its re-check commands

Measured by the dev on a real `AuthManager` (better-auth 1.7.3, organization plugin) over a real `ObjectQL` on a real `SqliteWasmDriver`, and pinned in `packages/client/src/auth-login-register-envelope.test.ts` so it can be re-driven rather than re-argued:

| reading | result | re-check |
|:--|:--|:--|

| what `/sign-in/email` answers | keys exactly `['redirect','token','user']` | same |
| any session in the response headers | **no header name matches `/session/i`**; `set-auth-token` is the signed token, and `SessionSchema.safeParse` of it fails | same |

⇒ the member cannot be produced from what these two calls return. ⛔ Not "hard" — **absent**.

## The question

`auth.login` / `auth.register` declare `data.session` and cannot deliver it. Which way does the disagreement get resolved?

## Options × real cost

| | what it does | what a caller feels |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **A** | `login()` / `register()` issue a **second** request to `GET /get-session` and merge its session into `data.session` | the declared type is delivered verbatim; the SDK's hottest path costs two round trips, and a login now **fails when the follow-up fails** — new failure semantics no ruling authorises today |
| **B** | narrow the declaration for these two methods (a sign-in/sign-up response whose `data` is `{ user, token }`), leaving `SessionResponse` to `/get-session` | no extra network call and the type finally describes what the routes really send; costs a `packages/spec` edit, an ADR-0087 disposition and a migration note, executed by the `domain:spec` seat |
| **C** | leave it as measured, pinned residue | zero risk today; the two methods keep advertising a member they never deliver, so a caller following the declared type to `result.data.session.expiresAt` still gets a **TypeError**, not a wrong value |

## 业务含义直译

- **A** = 为了让说明书上那一行成真,给每个登录的人加一趟来回。相当于产品手册印错了一个配件,于是每台出厂机器都多塞一个用不上的配件进去,还多一道可能装歪的工序。
- **B** = 承认说明书那一行印错了,改印。改版要走流程、要通知,但机器不动。
- **C** = 说明书继续印错的那版,反正"大部分人不会翻到那一页"。翻到的人会照着装,然后装不上。

## 四轴(业务立场)

- **① 项目长远合理性** —— B **缩小**特例:一个声明对应一种真实回包,两条路由不再共用一个它们只满足一半的形状。A 反过来把"多打一次请求"变成永久义务,为的是维持一个写错的承诺。C 让不一致无限期挂着,而且每多一个照着类型写的调用方,代价就长一分。
- **② 实际业务拉动** —— 今天谁撞上:任何照类型提示去取 `result.data.session.*` 的人,拿到的是崩溃(生产环境);而实测**没有任何一页已发布文档教人去读它**(`data.session` 全站 0 命中,对照词 3 命中)⇒ 拉动来自**类型提示**,不是来自文档或用户请求。A 的那次额外请求,是在为一个零文档引用的字段付每次登录的成本。
- **③ 防 AI 犯错** —— 出错时谁看到什么:B 让写错的人在**编译期**就被拒(类型里根本没有那个成员),是响亮拒绝。C 让他在**运行时**拿到 `TypeError`,而且是在用户点了登录之后 —— 静默承诺 + 晚爆。A 表面上都不报错,但把失败挪到"第二次请求挂了所以登录失败",错误现场和真实原因隔了一层,最难查。
- **④ 创业阶段不扩散** —— 「remove 优于 declare-and-maintain,每个已声明的键都是永久义务」。A 是把一个永久义务**再加一层实现负担**;B 是把一个从未兑现的义务**取消掉**;C 是把它继续欠着。B 是唯一一个让义务总量下降的。

## 推荐 + 回退 + 置信缺口

**推荐 B**,理由是四轴同向,且 Prime Directive #12 的那一问在这里有明确答案:这两条路由**真的没有 session**,所以是声明写错了而不是实现偷懒。**回退是 C** —— 如果你判断现在不值得动已发布契约,C 是安全的停车位,残留已经被测试钉住,随时可以再拿起来;⛔ 回退不是 A,因为 A 一旦落地就改变了登录的失败语义,回退它比回退 C 贵得多。
